Photoredox/Cobalt-Catalyzed Chemo-, Regio-, Diastereo- and
Enantioselective Reductive Coupling of 1,1-Disubstituted Allenes and
Cyclobutenes
Qianghui Wu, Zhihan Zhang, Qinglei Chong,* and Fanke Meng*
Abstract: A dual photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed protocol
for chemo-, regio-, diastereo- and enantioselective
reductive coupling of 1,1-disubstituted allenes and cyclo-
butenes through chemo-, regio-, diastereo- and enantio-
selective oxidative cyclization followed by stereoselec-
tive protonation promoted by a chiral phosphine–cobalt
complex is presented. Such process represents an
unprecedented reaction pathway for cobalt catalysis that
enables selective transformation of the less sterically
congested alkenes of 1,1-disubstituted allenes with cyclo-
butenes, incorporating a broad scope of tetrasubstituted
alkenes into the cyclobutane scaffolds in up to 86 %
yield, >98 : 2 chemo- and regioselectivity, >98 :2 dr and
>99.5:0.5 er. Functionalization delivered a variety of
enantioenriched cyclobutanes that are otherwise difficult
to access. Preliminary mechanistic studies revealed that
the reactions proceeded through oxidative cyclization
followed by protonation and protonation might be the
rate-determining step.

natural products and pharmaceutical important molecules,<sup>[1]</sup>
but also are useful intermediates and building blocks in
organic synthesis (Scheme 1a).<sup>[2]</sup> Therefore, establishment of
a general and modular strategy for catalytic enantioselective
synthesis of a broad scope of densely functionalized cyclo-
butanes is highly sought after. Although catalytic enantiose-
lective approaches for access to cyclobutanes include [2+2]
cycloaddition,<sup>[3]</sup> cyclization,<sup>[4]</sup> multistep ring contraction and
expansion reactions,<sup>[5]</sup> significant limitation on specific

Oxidative cyclization of two π-bonds promoted by low-
valent transition metal complexes represents a classical
elementary step in organometallic chemistry. Transition
metal-catalyzed transformations through oxidative cycliza-
tion constitutes one of the most important approaches for
carbon–carbon bond forming reactions in organic synthesis,
as such processes enable direct construction of carbon–
carbon bonds from easily accessible unsaturated hydro-
carbons without the requirement of pre-functionalization.<sup>[23]</sup>
In this context, most researches focused on catalytic
enantioselective reductive coupling of alkynes with alde-
hydes or activated alkenes through oxidative cyclization
promoted by Ni-<sup>[24]</sup> and Co-based<sup>[25]</sup> catalysts. In contrast to
reactions with alkynes that contain a single reactive site, it is
rare and more challenging for accurate control of the
chemo-, regio- and stereoselectivity of reactions with unsatu-
rated hydrocarbons bearing multiple reactive sites. Although
a few protocols for enantioselective coupling of 1,3-dienes
through oxidative coupling have been reported,<sup>[26]</sup> trans-
formations with allenes were far less developed. We
disclosed the only example of cobalt-catalyzed regiodiver-
gent enantioselective coupling of allenes and aldehydes
through oxidative cyclization.<sup>[27]</sup> However, approaches for
catalytic regio- and enantioselective reductive coupling of
allenes with cyclobutenes remained elusive. One of the key
challenges for such processes arises from the low reactivity
of the nonpolar cyclobutenes. The inherent lower-lying
LUMO of allenes results in preferential coordination to the
metal center and higher reactivity for oxidative cyclization.
Self-oligomerization of allenes has to be suppressed chemo-
selectively. Another crucial issue is accurate control of the
regio- and enantioselectivity. We envisioned that a proper
choice of chiral bisphosphine ligand combined with cobalt
catalysis might be able to effectively tune the chemo-, regio-
and enantioselectivity. Herein, we disclosed the first proto-
col for catalytic chemo-, regio- and enantioselective reduc-
tive coupling of 1,1-disubstituted allenes and cyclobutenes
through oxidative cyclization, incorporating a variety of
tetrasubstituted alkenyl groups and affording a broad scope
of enantioenriched cyclobutanes that are otherwise difficult
to access (Scheme 1c).

phine bearing a benzene backbone and chiral phospholane
fragments (4 d) were not able to promote the reaction

In conclusion, we have developed a photoredox/cobalt-
catalyzed protocol for chemo-, regio-, diastereo- and
enantioselective reductive coupling of 1,1-disubstituted
allenes and cyclobutenes to afford a broad scope of
enantioenriched cyclobutanes in high efficiency, chemo-,
regio- and stereoselectivity. To the best of our knowledge, it
is the first time that reductive coupling of allenes and
cyclobutenes through oxidative coupling pathway has been
disclosed. In addition, such process represented the first
example of generating hydroalkenylation products from
enantioselective functionalization of cyclobutenes. Prelimi-
nary mechanistic studies revealed that the reaction pro-
ceeded through chemo-, regio- and stereoselective oxidative
cyclization. Such discoveries unveiled a novel reaction path-
way for cobalt catalysis, opening new possibilities for design-
ing new transformations promoted by chiral cobalt-based
catalysts. Further investigations on cobalt-catalyzed enantio-
selective reactions through oxidative cyclization are under-
way.
